Laravel 12; prompts 0, MCP 0, Pint 1, Sail 1, PHPUnit 11. Follow project conventions; check sibling files when editing, use descriptive names, and reuse components. Do not create verification scripts or tinker when tests cover that functionality and prove it works. Stick to existing directory structure - don't create new base folders without approval. Do not change the application's dependencies without approval. You must only create documentation files if explicitly requested by the user.

Use Laravel Boost. Use `search-docs` before other approaches for Laravel-ecosystem documentation and before code changes; use broad topic queries, omit package names, and pass multiple queries when useful. Use `list-artisan-commands` to check Artisan parameters. Use `get-absolute-url` for project URLs, `tinker` to execute PHP or query Eloquent models, `database-query` for read-only database access, and `browser-logs` for recent browser logs only. If frontend changes are not reflected, ask the user to run `bun run build`, `bun run dev`, or `composer run dev`.

Always use curly braces for control structures. Use PHP 8 constructor property promotion; do not allow empty `__construct()` methods with zero parameters. Always use explicit return types and appropriate parameter types. Prefer PHPDoc blocks over comments. Never use comments within the code itself unless there is something _very_ complex going on. Add array shape types when appropriate; Enum keys are typically TitleCase.

Create files with `php artisan make:` commands; use `php artisan make:class` for generic PHP classes. Pass `--no-interaction` to all Artisan commands and correct options. Use Eloquent relationships with return types; prefer Eloquent/models over raw queries, avoid `DB::`, eager-load to prevent N+1s, and use the query builder for complex operations. Create useful factories and seeders for new models; ask if the user needs more, checking `php artisan make:model` options with `list-artisan-commands`. Use API Resources and versioning unless existing routes differ. Always create Form Request classes for validation, with rules and custom messages; follow sibling request conventions. Queue time-consuming work with `ShouldQueue`. Use Laravel authentication/authorization. Prefer named routes and `route()`. Use environment variables only in configuration files - never use the `env()` function directly outside of config files. Always use `config('app.name')`, not `env('APP_NAME')`. Use model factories and existing custom states in tests; follow project Faker conventions. Create tests with `php artisan make:test [options] {name}`; use `--unit` for unit tests. Most tests should be feature tests.
